description:
The Death Assistance for Registered Workers scheme is a significant welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to provide financial support to the families of registered workers in the unorganized sector. 

This scheme is specifically designed for workers who are registered under the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HBOCWWB). 

The scheme was officially launched on 1st January 2015. 

It aims to alleviate the financial burden on the families of deceased workers by providing them with a monetary benefit upon the worker's death. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to ensure that the families of registered workers receive timely financial assistance to cope with the loss of their breadwinner. 

The scheme targets to provide a one-time financial assistance of ₹2,00,000 to the families of registered workers who pass away. 

This assistance is intended to help cover immediate expenses such as funeral costs and other financial obligations that may arise due to the worker's death. 

The scheme is particularly beneficial for families that may not have adequate savings or insurance coverage to manage such unforeseen circumstances. 

To be eligible for the Death Assistance scheme, the worker must be registered with the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The worker must have a valid registration number and must have contributed to the welfare fund. 

There are no specific age limits for the registered workers under this scheme. 

However, the worker must have been actively engaged in building and other construction work at the time of their death. 

The family members of the deceased worker can apply for the assistance. 

Eligible family members include the spouse, children, or dependent relatives of the registered worker. 

The application process for the Death Assistance scheme is straightforward. 

The family members of the deceased worker must submit an application form to the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The application form can be obtained from the official website of the HBOCWWB or from their local offices. 

Along with the application form, the following documents are required: 

1. A copy of the death certificate of the registered worker. 
2. A copy of the worker's registration certificate with the HBOCWWB. 
3. Identity proof of the applicant such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 
4. Bank account details of the applicant for the disbursement of funds. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the officials of the HBOCWWB. 

The processing time for the application is typically around 30 days from the date of submission. 

Upon approval, the financial assistance of ₹2,00,000 will be disbursed directly to the bank account of the eligible family member. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Government of Haryana to enhance the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector. 

The HBOCWWB was established to provide various welfare measures for construction workers in the state. 

As of October 2023, the HBOCWWB has registered over 6 lakh workers under its welfare schemes. 

The board has also been actively promoting awareness about the various benefits available to registered workers and their families. 

In addition to the Death Assistance scheme, the HBOCWWB offers several other welfare schemes such as maternity benefits, medical assistance, and education assistance for children of registered workers. 

The implementation of the Death Assistance scheme is overseen by the Haryana Labour Department. 

The department is responsible for ensuring that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries in a timely manner. 

The contact details for the Haryana Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board are available on their official website. 

The board also provides a helpline for workers and their families to inquire about the status of their applications. 

The initiative has been well-received by the public, with many families expressing gratitude for the financial support during difficult times. 

The scheme has also contributed to raising awareness about the importance of registering as a worker under the HBOCWWB. 

This registration not only provides access to the Death Assistance scheme but also to other welfare benefits. 

The government has been actively promoting the registration of workers to ensure that they can avail themselves of these benefits. 

As of 2023, the Haryana government has allocated a budget of ₹50 crores for the implementation of various welfare schemes under the HBOCWWB. 

This allocation reflects the government's commitment to improving the living standards of construction workers and their families. 

The Death Assistance scheme is an essential part of this commitment, providing crucial support to families in their time of need. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's recognition of the challenges faced by workers in the unorganized sector. 

It highlights the need for social security measures to protect the livelihoods of vulnerable populations. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can significantly ease the burden on families who may be struggling to cope with the loss of their primary earner. 

In conclusion, the Death Assistance for Registered Workers scheme is a vital welfare initiative that aims to provide financial support to the families of deceased workers in the construction sector. 

With a one-time assistance of ₹2,00,000, the scheme addresses the immediate financial needs of families during a challenging time. 

The eligibility criteria and straightforward application process ensure that the benefits reach those who need them the most. 

Overall, the scheme reflects the government's ongoing efforts to enhance the welfare of workers in the unorganized sector and provide them with a safety net in times of crisis.
